newsitem.title: UK: Wickes says operating loss for first 9 mos.
newsitem.headline: Wickes says operating loss for first 9 mos.

text.p: Wickes Plc, the troubled Do-It-Yourself retailer, finally revealed the financial implications of accounting irregularities, reporting that corrections and charges had pushed it into loss for the first nine months of the year.

The loss, mentioned in a letter to shareholders explaining the implications of the problem, was not quantified, however. But the 1995 results will be hit by writeoffs against shareholder funds as well as property related charges. Like for like sales in the period were up 1.2 percent on 1995.
The low like-for-like growth reflected a very severe downturn in sales for the first quarter, which was 9.7 percent lower than 1995 levels.
But a steady recovery was seen in the second and third quarters. The third quarter like for like growth was 8.9 percent.

The chairman Michael von Brentano's letter to shareholders said that the nine month loss stemmed from corrections to the results which related to supplier payments which were inaccurately accounted for. Profitability was also hit by exceptional costs stemming from rationalisation actions.
The chairman said the group was now working on a new business plan to help it recover from its problems.

"A new business plan... will be finalised once the negotiations with suppliers are substantially complete. This provides for a substantial reduction in costs, improved marketing initiatives and efficient administrative procedures."
The board's aim was to return the group to profitability in 1997, said von Brentano.
